sentences.text:
The present petition has been filed challenging the suspension order Annexure P/2 dated 06.06.2024.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the order Annxure P/2 has been passed in colourable exercise of powers because the order though is signed by the Manager of the Society but in second paragraph of the said order, it is mentioned that this order is being passed as per the decision taken in the meeting dated 06.06.2024 by Administrator of the Society.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that prior to that a letter dated 05.06.2024 was issued to the petitioner by the Administrator of the Society and as per that letter it was mentioned that there was a meeting taken by the Collector who is Administrator of the Bank (the society of the petitioner is a Primary society and member society of the Cooperative Bank which in itself is also a cooperative society) i.e. the Collector of the District wherein it has been directed that there is very less progress of the recovery of loans in the society and therefore, strict action be taken in the matter of recovery of loan 2 WP-16757-2024 failing which disciplinary action shall be initiated against the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that one hand on 05.06.2024 petitioner was asked about speedy progress of recovery of loan but on the very next date the petitioner has been placed under suspension.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has admitted that there is no remedy of any appeal against the suspension order as per service regulations applicable to the society and a dispute can be raised before the Registrar and the Registrar in case of his society would be Deputy Registrar and the dispute can be raised in terms of Section 55(2) of the M.P. Cooperative Society Act but since first line of first paragraph of Annexure P/1 mentions that directions to initiate disciplinary action have been received from Deputy Registrar, hence, there would be no utility in filing dispute before the Deputy Registrar itself.

sentences.text: It is further contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the order has been passed by the administrator of the society whereas the service regulation mentions that it is the Manager who is the disciplinary authority of the petitioner and thus the order having been passed by the higher authority, is bad in law.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that it is the manager who has in fact signed the suspension order and this order should be reckoned to be issued by the Manager itself and the reference to administrator of the society is by clumsily drafting the order Annexure P/2.
It is further contended that in the cooperative Bank there are 178 members societies and the society in question is at 176th position in the matter of recovery.
By referring to Annexure R-5/1, it is contended that there is a progress of 1.05 percent against over dues loans and zero percent against the current loan.

Learned counsel for the respondents have further argued that 3 WP-16757-2024 the charge-sheet has already been issued to the petitioner on 14.06.2024 vide Annexure R-5/2 and now at this stage it would not be proper to reinstate the petitioner because the departmental enquiry against the petitioner would be affected if he is reinstated on the post.

Learned counsel for respondents have further submitted that past conduct of the petitioner has not been good because he was involved in the cases under prevention of corruption Act and also under Section 376 of IPC and POCSO Act.
However, no such documents have been filed along with reply.

6. Heard.
7 .
The matter relates to reference to two administrators, one is the administrator of the Bank and other is administrator is of the Primary society in which the petitioner is a employee.
This society is member society of the Bank.
The administrator of Bank is the District Collector and Administrator of the society in which the petitioner is employee is some other officer of the cooperative Department.
8. The issue of order having been passed by higher authority is taken up first.
The parties are at consensus in submitting that there is no remedy of appeal as per the service regulations.

If the order is considered to have been passed by the Manager then no appeal lies to the Administrator and if the order is considered to have passed by Administrator also then also there is no further appeal as per service regulation.

In either events, it is conceded by both the parties that the matter would be agitated in accordance with provisions of M.P. Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 before the statutory authority of Cooperative Department under the said Act.

9. The legality of an order passed by Higher Authority was considered by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of 1997 (3) SCC 371 and it has been held as under:-

namely, Zonal Manager, who alone is competent to remove him, the order of dismissal passed by the Managing Director is bad in law.

In support thereof, he placed reliance on a judgment of this Court in Surjit Ghosh v. Chairman & Managing Director, United Commercial Bank [(1995) 2 SCC 474 : 1995 SCC (L&S) 529 : (1995)

sentences.text: It is an admitted position that as a joint enquiry was conducted against all the delinquent officials, the highest in the hierarchy of competent authority who could take disciplinary action against the delinquents was none other than the Managing Director of the Corporation.
In normal circumstances the Managing Director being the appellate authority should not pass the order of punishment so as to enable the delinquent employee to avail of right of appeal.
It is now a well- settled legal position that an authority lower than the appointing authority cannot take any decision in the matter of disciplinary action.
But there is no prohibition in law that the higher authority should not take decision or impose the penalty as the primary authority in the matter of disciplinary action.
On that basis, it cannot be said that there will be discrimination violating Article 14 of the Constitution or causing material prejudice.

In the judgment relied on by the counsel,
it would appear that in the Rules, officer lower in hierarchy was the disciplinary authority but the appellate authority had passed the order removing the officer from service.
Thereby, the appellate remedy provided under the Rules was denied.

In those circumstances, this Court opined that it caused prejudice to the delinquent as he would have otherwise availed of the appellate remedy and his right to consider his case by an appellate authority on question of fact was not available.
But it cannot be laid as a rule of law that in all circumstances the higher authority should consider and decide the case imposing penalty as a primary authority under the Rules.

In this case,
a right of second appeal/revision also was provided to the Board.
In fact, appeal was preferred to the Board.
The Board elaborately considered the matter through the Chairman.
It is not 5 WP-16757-2024 violative of Article 14 of the Constitution."

10. In Goa Shipyard Ltd. v. Babu Thomas, 2007 (10) SCC 662 , the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:-
"15.

sentences.text: Mr Rao next referred to the amended CDA Rules wherein it has been provided that for all officers up to and inclusive of Manager, the disciplinary authority who can impose major penalties is the General Manager/Functional Director and the appellate authority is the Chairman & Managing Director.

According to Mr Rao, since the order of dismissal has been issued by the Chairman & Managing Director who is an appellate authority, the respondent has been deprived of his right of appeal to the Chairman & Managing Director.

According to him, under the amended CDA Rules the appellate authority is the Chairman & Managing Director but as the major penalty has been imposed by the Chairman & Managing Director, he cannot act as an appellate authority and therefore the respondent has lost one form of remedy available to him.
We are unable to countenance to this submission.
The respondent was not denied the right of appeal.

Undisputedly, the respondent filed an appeal before the Board of Directors, as the order of dismissal was passed by the CMD, and the Board of Directors considered his appeal and by a detailed order dismissed the appeal on 27- 9-1997.

In fact, the Board of Directors independently considered the Vijay Kumar Dubey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67472801/
3 appeal and while dismissing the appeal held that Charges (ii), (v), (x)(a), (x)(b), (xi)
and (xiii) are not fully or entirely proved and confirmed the dismissal order on Charges (i), (vi), (vii), (x)(c) and (xii).

sentences.text: The appeal was considered independently by the appellate authority and a detailed order passed after application of mind.

In such circumstances, we are clearly of the view that no prejudice whatsoever has been caused to the respondent as he availed an opportunity of an appeal before the Board of Directors as an appellate authority."
11.

As in the present case the even if the order is deemed to be passed by an Administrator as mentioned in the Annexure P/2, does not effect the remedy of appeal available to the petitioner,
because there is no such remedy 6 WP-16757-2024 in either case.
Thus, the order cannot be quashed only on the ground of it having been passed by a higher authority.
As per section 48 (2) of the M.P. Cooperative Societies Act 1960, management of every society vests in a Board of Directors.

As per section 53 (3) and (5) of the said Act, in absence of Board, the Administrator exercises the powers of the Board as may be required in the interest of the society, subject to control of the Registrar and manages the affairs of the society.
The Administrator has taken the place of Board of Directors in absence of Board and thus, the administrator also exercised control over the petitioner and is not alien to the society.
Thus, the order cannot be quashed on the ground that it has been passed by a higher authority.

12. So far as the contention made regarding the order having been passed at the instance of Dy.
Registrar is concerned, as per Section 53 of M.P. Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 in case of supersession of Board of Director, the administrator has to remain under the control of the Registrar and the Registrar is having power to give instruction to the administrator from time to time.

The relevant is as under:-
53 (3) The administrator so appointed, shall subject to the control of the Registrar and to such instructions as he may, from time to time, give, have power to exercise all or any of the powers and to discharge all or any of the functions of the Board of Directors or of any officer of the society and to take all such actions, as may be required in the interest of the society.
13.
Thus, the order cannot be said to be bad in law merely on the ground that some instructions of the Collector were forwarded by the Deputy Registrar to the Administrator.
The Administrator has to work under the control of the Registrar and the Registrar is having powers to issue instructions to the Administrator.

Thus, even if the impugned order is deemed to be passed at the instance of the Deputy Registrar, then also in 7 WP-16757-2024 terms of section 53 (3), the Registrar of the society is having powers to issue instructions to and exercise control over the Administrator in absence of the elected Board.

14. In case the order is passed under the directions of the Dy. Registrar and the order as stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner is deemed to be passed by Dy. Registrar himself, even then the petitioner has a remedy under Section 78 of M.P. Cooperative Societies Act 1960 to file an appeal before the Registrar.

The relevant Section 78 as under:-

( 1) Save where it has been otherwise provided, an appeal shall lie from every original order under this Act or the rules made thereunder:-
(a) if such order is passed by any officer subordinate to Registrar, other than Additional Registrar or Joint Registrar, whether or not the Officer passing the order is invested with the powers of the Registrar, to the Registrar;
(b) if such order is passed by the Registrar, Additional Registrar or a Joint Registrar,
to the Tribunal."

15. Thus, even if the order Annexure P/2 is deemed to be passed on the instructions of the Deputy Registrar in terms of the Section 53(3) & (5) of the Act of 1960 even then the petitioner has a remedy of appeal before the Registrar.

16. As this Court has reached to a finding that the order Annexure P/2 does not suffer from any vice of jurisdiction and there is availability of alternative remedy to the petitioner against the said order Annexure P/2, this Court refrains from making any comments on the merits of the case vis-a-vis the allegations against the petitioner which were argued by the respondents, lest it may prejudice the right of the petitioner in appeal and also prejudice the enquiry pending against the petitioner.
8 WP-16757-2024 17. Resultantly, interference is declined.
The petitioner is set at liberty to prefer appeal under Section 78 of the M.P. Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 before the Registrar.

If such an appeal is filed before the Registrar within a period of three weeks from today, then the period spent in prosecuting the petition shall not be taken into account while reckoning limitation.
18. With the aforesaid petition is disposed of.
